title: How to get your first 10,000 LinkedIn followers: one mission, one profile, consistent good posts
summary: Ruben argues that LinkedIn growth comes from writing good, targeted posts around one clear mission, not from pods, automations or AI comment spam. He covers profile setup (headline, featured link, experience section) and a Mission + Solution + Angle + Format post framework. The essay is paywalled, so the step-by-step 0 to 10,000 plan is not visible.

principles.text: Pick one problem to solve and nothing else; if it can't be said in one sentence, it's too broad.
principles.quote: That's it. Solve one problem. And one ONLY.

principles.text: A mission you can't state in one sentence signals a lack of focus.
principles.quote: If you can’t explain it within one sentence, you need help.

principles.text: Win with good posts (targeted, helpful, consistent, improving), not shortcuts like pods, cold automations or AI comments.
principles.quote: Good is targeted. Good is helpful. Good is consistent and gets better.

principles.text: Each post is one solution to the mission, built from solution, angle and format.
principles.quote: Post = one (of the many) solutions to the one problem.

principles.text: Make your headline your mission with a cheeky, clear twist.
principles.quote: Your mission is your headline, with a twist.

principles.text: Keep the featured section to one link and no description to cut friction and lift conversions.
